key_insight: Twisted SrTiO3 membranes exhibit a reconstructed moiré interface with polar distortions, modified Ti electronic structure, and enhanced microwave admittance.
engineering_relevance: Controlled interface termination could enable emergent electrical behavior in perovskite oxides, but this study does not demonstrate AI methods or solar-cell performance.
method: Stack atomically flat SrTiO3 membranes with a twist.
Establish a predominantly SrO–TiO2 interfacial configuration.
Directly visualize buried-interface reconstruction and characterize electrical signatures.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports moiré-periodic reconstruction distinct from rigid-stacking geometry, head-to-head-like polar distortions, moiré-modulated Ti electronic structure, and enhanced microwave admittance.
watch_item: Surface contamination, roughness, and mixed terminations can complicate interface identification and control.
paper_title: Moiré reconstruction at a twisted SrTiO3 interface
